title: Wilson Pickett Estate Partners With Primary Wave in Deal That Includes NIL Rights & Publishing Stake
summary: The soul legend's hits include "In the Midnight Hour," "Mustang Sally" and “634-5789 (Soulsville, U.S.A.).”
contentText:
Primary Wave is partnering with the estate of Wilson Pickett in a deal that includes sharing in the legendary singer’s name, image and likeness rights and also apparently a stake in his music publishing catalog. The estate will work closely with Primary Wave on new marketing, branding, digital and synch opportunities as well as film and TV projects, according to the Wednesday (Sept. 2) announcement, which did not disclose terms of the deal.

While Pickett, who died at age 64 in 2006, often sang songs by other songwriters, he also did have a hand in writing some of the songs he recorded, including co-writes with such legendary soul music writers as Steve Cropper (“In The Midnight Hour”), Bobby Womack, and David Porter and Homer Banks (“I’m Drifting”). He even shared a co-write with late music industry executive Jerry Wexler (“Soul Dance Number Three”). The Songview database gives Pickett a songwriting credit on some 100 songs.

“Promoting my brother’s incredible legacy has not just been a responsibility; it has been a labor of absolute love,” said Pickett estate executive Max Pickett in a statement. “Wilson poured his soul into every lyric, leaving us a musical inheritance that belongs to the world. Since his passing, it has been my sacred mission to ensure that his voice continues to echo for generations to come. I am profoundly grateful to partner with Primary Wave — stewards who truly understand the weight of his history and the timeless power of his sound. Together, we are keeping the Wicked Pickett’s fire burning bright.”

Besides “In the Midnight Hour,” Pickett’s smash hit songs as an artist include “Mustang Sally,” his cover of “Land of 1,000 Dances, “634-5789 (Soulsville, U.S.A.)” and his cover of “Funky Broadway.”

“Primary Wave is honored to partner with Max Pickett and the Pickett family to help preserve and expand the legacy of one of the most influential artists in music history,” Primary Wave’s David Weitzman added in a statement. “Wilson Pickett was a once in a generation talent, an iconic soul singer, electrifying performer, and one of the defining voices of American music. His remarkable body of work, created alongside legendary collaborators including Jerry Wexler, the Stax Records team, the Muscle Shoals Rhythm Section, and Gamble & Huff, helped shape the sound of soul and R&B for generations. We are proud to celebrate his extraordinary career and ensure that his legacy continues to reach new audiences for years to come.”
